sections.heading: Stefano's Published Work
sections.summary: Stefano published his full work with benchmarks; everything is implemented except the Ledger app, and he offered to present it at a future session.
sections.body:
- Stefano's work is now published. It is roughly 200 pages with full benchmarks and differs a lot from the version presented on an earlier call.
  - The spirit is the same. Since last time the team patched and optimized it and moved to "Flock", which Stefano said made a huge difference.
- Everything is implemented except the Ledger app, which is pending cleanup and expected around the end of the week.
- Stefano offered to present at the next session. Antonio said they would see how things evolve, since the call format may change.

sections.heading: Move to Discord and Daisugi Migration
sections.summary: Most PQ discussion has moved to Discord, where core devs are now engaged; PandaOps migrated Daisugi, which still needs a restart to adopt sphincs.art parameters.
sections.body:
- Most conversation has moved to Discord, and core devs are now much more engaged.
  - Channels: [pq-el](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1569690395095470130), [Daisugi thread](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1572742161932484798), [pq-networking](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1569690422010191873), [pq-cl](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1569690373633216644), [pq-general](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1398301046085914745).
  - The call format will shift toward fewer presentations and more decision-making.
  - At the close, Antonio said he will probably close the Telegram channel. Next call is in two weeks.
- Philip (PandaOps) migrated Daisugi to a more professionalized environment with more nodes and more transactions.
  - Project 11 and Nethermind helped with the transition.
- Daisugi is still running an older parameter set, not the sphincs.art defaults.
  - The latest Nethermind branch is already updated to the sphincs.art parameters. The network needs a restart after pushing that branch.
  - Antonio asked the Nethermind team to ping PK after the call to restart with sphincs.art parameters so benchmarking can begin.

sections.heading: Aggregation Roadmap for Hegota
sections.summary: lightclient and others expect no aggregation in Hegota (Matteo disagreed); the next devnet runs without it, and aggregation stays the long-term goal.
sections.body:
- Daisugi previously ran builder aggregation and a version of 8288.
  - The block builder aggregated about 20 signatures per second.
- Kev proposed (on Discord) a three-stage approach:
  1. Benchmark raw signatures with no aggregation.
  2. Move back to block builder aggregation.
  3. Eventually move to mempool aggregation.
- lightclient's position:
  - Aggregation is something to support in the future, but it will not happen in Hegota.
  - The EL must be ready to carry a non-trivial number of signatures without aggregation.
  - The CL must have aggregation for leanXMSS. The EL can be more relaxed about forcing it because of its many implications.
- Matteo argued aggregation in Hegota is feasible if it only aggregates leanSPHINCS, with no other signatures or proofs. He said Nethermind has done something similar.
- Points raised in chat:
  - soispoke questioned the builder aggregation path as a big departure from current protocol guarantees. He asked whether it is safer to ship a first PQ EL without aggregation, accepting far fewer PQ txs per block.
  - Ryan McPeck: close to 0% chance of shipping aggregation in H*.
  - Tom Wambsgans: leanVM currently aggregates 700 leanSphincs signatures (sphincs.art default params) per second on an M4 Max.
  - Iván: aggregation is possible. The open question is when leanVM is production-ready enough to put in the protocol.
  - Mario Vega: turning aggregation on should ideally be completely transparent to users.
  - Toni Wahrstätter: with 8288, the hope is to scale gradually as async aggregation improves.
- Antonio noted that leanVM can be shipped either way, since it supports both aggregated and non-aggregated verification.
- Guru's summary in chat: the call decided against aggregation for the next devnet.
  - Stefan asked whether that meant builder or mempool aggregation. Guru answered neither.

sections.heading: leanSPHINCS Parameter Selection
sections.summary: sphincs.art default parameters stay for the testnet; Nico will propose alternative parameter sets for comparison, with no exotic optimizations.
sections.body:
- Nico said the chosen parameters were the most conservative option and optimized for nothing in particular.
  - They have a very high lifetime and lean toward MPC friendliness: many small FORS rather than tall ones.
  - That makes them less permutation-friendly and therefore less aggregation-friendly.
  - Nico claims at least 15-20% fewer hashes with the same signature size and lifetime by trading FORS shape. He claims 30-40% from further regular parameter changes.
- Antonio said sphincs.art did optimize somewhat for a low number of verification hashes, which suits aggregation, at the cost of signature size.
  - If aggregation is dropped, he questioned whether sphincs.art is still the right parameter set and would instead optimize for size.
- Nico raised a Safe constraint: the Safe Transaction Service backend requires signatures under 5 KB.
  - The backend could be changed, but it is a significant change.
  - In chat, Nico added that he needs an audited verifier with Safe securing billions and does not want months of churn.
- lightclient was surprised the signature grew from 4 KB (in Mumbai) to 8 KB and asked what trade-offs caused it.
  - Antonio: mainly the lifetime increase from 2^24 to 2^30.
  - Matteo: the 4 KB version used one bigger tree that requires users to prune it. Per the last call, pruning was judged undesirable for several reasons:
    - risk;
    - fewer signatures per device and longer keygen;
    - loss of privacy when signing.
  - Nico disagreed that pruning is risky or loses privacy:
    - Hardware manufacturers' security teams called it orders of magnitude simpler than other solutions and their preferred option.
    - Proof-of-concept apps for Trezor and Ledger keep about 1,000 signatures private.
    - He also said two- or three-layer trees could work.
  - Nico (chat): pruning is a signer-only change, the signature is identical, and it does not affect aggregation. It only matters for constrained hardware wallets.
- Matteo: the hash function is now decided, and much of the scheme is set in stone.
  - Shrinking signatures, e.g. by changing the Winternitz parameter, increases verification hashes and slows aggregation.
  - He disputed Nico's "bigger FORS, reduce h" approach, saying it raises signature size. Nico will send concrete parameter sets.
- Antonio's proposal:
  - Use the sphincs.art defaults agreed last month on the testnet. They are already implemented in leanVM, Nethermind and wallets.
  - Benchmark them. Being near the worst case on size means things can only improve.
  - Nico should propose alternative parameters in parallel for comparison.
  - Condition: no exotic or experimental optimizations for now. Nico agreed those are a separate later debate.
- Nico asked that core devs doing the production work take project-management oversight. He worries that continued delay will leave too little time.
  - Antonio: switching SPHINCS variants is a small change for client devs.
- Stefano: changing parameters is easy, but designing around a given signature size can drive design choices that are harder to undo.
- soispoke warned against a loop of "freeze for devnets, change later". Devnet metrics on parameters that will change say little about throughput or node resources.
  - Antonio disagreed: devnets are always useful, there is currently no data at all, and changing once or twice is acceptable.
- Iván (ethrex): EL clients just need a concrete SPHINCS variant to start building and measuring.
  - Antonio pointed to the [sphincs.art](https://sphincs.art/) defaults as the decided set.
- Chat discussion:
  - Nico: leanSPHINCS is the SPHINCS- variant being canonized, now identical after the decision to use Keccak. Reference repo: [SPHINCs-](https://github.com/nconsigny/SPHINCs-) (see leansphincs-s / leansphincs-f).
  - Project Eleven shared a [SPHINCS parameter tool](https://research.projecteleven.com/tools/sphincs-parameter).
  - soispoke reported that shrinking the signature means slower aggregation and/or slower signing. The floor is about 2x smaller, roughly 4 kB.
  - soispoke also asked for a write-up of why the parameters were chosen. Nico will share articles.
  - lightclient suggested choosing a size that is nice today and an aggregation speed that is a little painful today, expecting aggregation to keep improving.
  - lightclient asked how much better aggregation is at 8 KB vs 4 KB. This was not answered on the call.
  - Maria Silva and Iván: since aggregation is still the end goal, parameters should be optimized for it even if Hegota ships without it. Kev partly agreed.
  - Barnabas argued aggregation is essential.

sections.heading: Block Size and Networking Without Aggregation
sections.summary: Per-byte pricing keeps worst-case block size unchanged, but large PQ signatures cut throughput; supporting more PQ txs needs larger blocks and networking improvements.
sections.body:
- Antonio's concern: signatures grow from 64 bytes to about 6.4-7 KB, more than 100x. With fixed block size, far fewer transactions fit per block.
- lightclient: limits can be raised.
  - Better block and transaction gossip, plus possibly higher bandwidth requirements in this extraordinary case, make 2-4 MB blocks reasonable.
  - Networking folks generally consider that range fine. A 30 MB block could not propagate in 12 seconds.
  - 500 txs with one 8 KB signature each is about 4 MB, plus roughly half a megabyte of other data.
  - Today's max block is about 1.2 MB and the average is about 400 KB.
  - Proposed improvement: separate witness/signature propagation. Nodes would pull signatures already seen in their mempool instead of re-propagating them after the block is produced. Mempool gossip efficiency then becomes the focus.
- Gottfried Herold: part of a SPHINCS signature can be independent of the message, so it could be pre-propagated.
- Toni Wahrstätter: every byte is priced (64 gas per byte), so worst-case block size does not change.
  - Larger transactions limit throughput unless the gas limit scales.
  - Today's block size limit is 8MB on the uncompressed RLP. At 200 million gas the EL block can reach about 6MB uncompressed, roughly 2 megabytes compressed.
  - The protocol is ready, but better networking is needed for a 5MB average block.
- lightclient: block size needs to increase some, which requires networking improvements.
  - Stefan asked whether new networking code is being tested. lightclient said work is needed and people are working on it.
- Throughput measurements shared in chat:
  - Iván measured about 115 txs per block with ~8kb leanSPHINCS frame txs vs ~2.8k secp256k1 frame txs, in an implementation of [EIPs PR #12672](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12672).
  - In another experiment he fit ~100 frame-leanSPHINCS txs in Glamsterdam blocks vs ~2,5k frame-secp256k1 txs.
- Expected adoption and pricing (chat):
  - Nico: PQ will not be 100% of transactions, expected 5-10% at the beginning.
  - Justin Florentine suggested pricing PQ txs higher to discourage unnecessary adoption.
  - jochem-brouwer noted [EIP-2780](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2780) lowers the minimum tx cost from 21k to 15k. Signature size could be built into intrinsic gas, which he then noted is already part of tx cost.

sections.heading: Single User Migration Requirement
sections.summary: Broad agreement that users should migrate to PQ signatures once; Justin Florentine was open to two variants if aggregation proves incompatible.
sections.body:
- Matteo asked whether users would migrate twice: once to non-aggregation parameters, then again when aggregation arrives with different optimized parameters.
- lightclient: this must happen one time. Asking users to switch PQ schemes twice is untenable and would be a failure.
  - Hegota should plan around no aggregation, but parameters should be balanced rather than fully optimized for aggregation.
- Agreement in chat: "we definitely don't want 2 variants" (lightclient), with broad support from Iván, Tom Wambsgans, Mario Vega, Guru, soispoke, Pablo, Matteo and Nico.
  - Justin Florentine was open to shipping twice if aggregation turns out incompatible with non-aggregation.
  - soispoke: fix the scheme as soon as possible so it can be relied on as a fixed primitive.

sections.heading: Process for Choosing Mainnet Parameters
sections.summary: Kev asked for a defined process and question list for choosing mainnet SPHINCS parameters; no process was agreed, and Nico stressed the end-of-January deadline.
sections.body:
- Kev: everyone agrees the end state is a SPHINCS variant. What is missing is a process for choosing between parameter sets. Without one, devnets risk being wasted work.
  - Open questions he listed:
    - Whether networking can handle the larger signatures.
    - MPC wallet readiness.
    - Wallet outreach.
    - Whether 8 KB vs 4 KB is a blocker.
    - Aggregation speed, for forward compatibility with leanVM aggregation.
- Antonio: the first question is whether networking and block size can support signatures more than 100x larger.
  - SPHINCS has no win-win; every gain is paid for elsewhere: lifetime vs size, verification vs size.
  - The parameters were chosen with aggregation in mind. The shift to no aggregation happened about two days ago, and revisiting takes time.
- Kev: the defaults were tentative. Picking a process is orthogonal to the devnet, and Bogota devnet 3 does not need a finalized parameter set.
- Nico: little was learned in the month since choosing the most conservative set.
  - The deadline is end of January, and December holidays reduce capacity.
  - He urged moving directly to more production-realistic parameters.
- Antonio: better to move with the existing set than stand still. Changing once or twice on a testnet is acceptable.
- Decision deferred: no process agreed. Discussion continues on Discord.

sections.heading: Bogota Devnet 3 Integration
sections.summary: Consensus to put leanSPHINCS on the next Bogota devnet instead of Daisugi; the PROOF frame vs signature list choice remains open and blocks the spec.
sections.body:
- Kev asked for specs rather than jumping to testnets.
  - He expected something like an execution specs PR on top of a Bogota devnet.
  - Concrete proposal: branch on top of Bogota devnet 2 adding leanSPHINCS via a PROOF frame or signature list, with no Daisugi.
- Antonio agreed. Daisugi was built for aggregation, so it is no longer needed if aggregation is off.
- lightclient: leanSPHINCS and frames are on the critical path and belong on the next Bogota devnets.
  - This is past the experimental stage. Devnet 3 should be as close as possible to what Frames will look like on mainnet.
  - PROOF frame vs signature list is still being decided.
- Agreement: Bogota devnet 3 should include leanSPHINCS plus whatever structure holds the signature.
  - Parameters: Antonio wants the current sphincs.art defaults; Kev said any SPHINCS parameter set works for the devnet.
  - Chat: Guru, Iván, Stefan and Justin agreed it should be Bogota devnet 3.
  - Iván noted it may be a later Bogota devnet since selfdestruct still needs to be reactivated.
- Guru (chat): devnet 3 can start as soon as PROOF frame vs signature list and the related spec details are decided. This is for EL devs to settle.
  - Mario Vega suggested signature list, since PROOF is new, signature list is tested, and the devnet has no aggregation.
  - Guru: if there is consensus on PROOF, include it.
  - Kev asked where this decision will be made. Antonio proposed continuing on Discord.
- Iván (ethrex) is writing execution spec tests for one alternative. A working implementation is available in the `pq-el-devnet-0` branches for anyone who wants to start measuring.
- Mario Vega asked for specs to make devnets more predictable and easier to coordinate.
